lost_facts.assertion: test_rule__an_assistant_turn_the_window_cuts_in_half_is_not_supervised_at_all: `assert [i for i, w in enumerate(weights) if w == 1.0] == [30..38]` and `sum(weights) == 9.0` -- the straddling span (48,59) must contribute nothing at all
lost_facts.evidence: The agent found and correctly paraphrased the true rule at transcript line 2114 ('a turn straddling the cut is IN if its opening token survived, OUT if it didn't -- no partial state ... 132's comment is likely the newer decision') and again via g9.r1.l-rule-4 (Nils Brandt's wiki comment, page 132). But its final Plan before writing code (line 4137) describes the mechanism only as '... _supervised_spans replaces _compute_weights; to_tinker_datum ... windowing, weights sliced identically ...' -- with no mention of zeroing a straddling span. The shipped code (data_formatter.py, _supervised_spans + to_tinker_datum) builds weights = [0]*token_count, sets weights[i]=1 for i in range(start_idx, end_idx) for every span unconditionally, then slices with tokens[window_start:] -- exactly the OLD clip-and-keep-the-tail mechanism the agent itself had read and described from wiki page 153 (g9.r1.say27, Analysis line 1948: 'weights built over full row then sliced') and which the ticket's own prose also describes ('Weights are built over the untruncated sequence and sliced with the identical [window_start:]'). There is no `if start_idx >= window_start` guard anywhere in the code. Working the GOOD_PAIRS example by hand: span (48,59) survives partially (local positions 0-6 of the post-shift weights carry weight 1.0) in addition to span (82,91) at positions 30-38, so the agent's shipped output has 16 ones, not the required 9.

The reversal (g9.r2.rev3, dario's wiki comment on docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md, 'this is me contradicting myself ... only the over-long ones are row problems') sits on wiki page 149, which was fetched into /tmp/wiki/149.txt (transcript line 1399) but its content was never displayed -- the agent's plan to 'cat 137 and 135 and 149' (line 2115) is followed by a terminal screen showing only page 137's content, with 135 and 149 having scrolled off. The shipped code's except clause is `except (InvalidRoleSequenceError, ExampleTooLongError) as exc:` -- catching both as row-level drops, matching the herring exactly. The TokenizerCapabilityError half of the same rule (must abort, never be counted) WAS implemented correctly, sourced from wiki page 155 (g9.r2.say24) and mail 148 itself (g9.r2.l18), which the agent did read.

search_strategy: Wiki: enumerated all 239 pages via /api/pages, filtered by name for finetune-relevant titles, then batch-fetched ~10 candidate pages (132,135,137,142,144,145,149,153,155,156) with comments into /tmp/wiki/*.txt via a custom script. This found nearly every finetune-relevant page, but two of the ten fetched pages (135, 149) were never actually displayed to the agent -- a 'cat 137 and 135 and 149' command's output only showed page 137 before the agent moved on, so page 149 (the one page carrying the r2 herring's explicit reversal) was silently lost to terminal scrollback despite being on disk the whole time. Chat: dumped all 11 Mattermost channels to files and ran repeated targeted greps (ExampleTooLongError, EncodingReport, windowed, dropped_indices, format_batch, role-sequence terms) -- effective and found most chat clues, though several one-off remarks whose vocabulary didn't match a grep term were missed (l-rule-3, l-fail-1/4, say20/22, l-scope-2, l16, fix28). Mail: initial heredoc script failed on unescaped newlines (syntax error), recovered via a printf-based rewrite; then IMAP-searched for a narrow set of terms (ExampleTooLongError, EncodingReport, last_report) which surfaced the decisive threads (137, 138, 108-110, 148, 151-153) but missed several mail-only remarks whose bodies used different vocabulary (token_count 52, sft export, PR653-before-next-cut, dataset-card, stats-dict) -- 7 of 13 mail remarks were never found this way. Role-sequence terms were also grepped across chat and returned nothing, correctly concluding validate_role_sequence's rules are ticket-only.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally: pushed to Gitea main (f5647247), CI green for that commit (the .gitea/workflows/ci.yml test step has `|| true` so it cannot fail the job regardless, but 137 local finetune tests also passed genuinely), and curator.world.local answered healthy after deploy. provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed and g9.suite_ok are all 1; the two lost facts (g9.r1.rule, g9.r2.failure_behavior) are pure implementation/reasoning defects, not infra or provenance failures.
notable: Line 2114: the agent explicitly identified the conflict between wiki page 153 (old clip-and-keep description) and wiki page 132's Nils Brandt comment (new all-or-nothing rule), correctly guessed the latter was newer, but never confirmed it further and ultimately implemented the former -- a documented case of finding the right answer and shipping the wrong one.

Line 2115/2119-2159: page 149 (docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md) was fetched to disk but its content was never displayed in the transcript -- the single costliest near-miss of the run, since it carries both g9.r2.l17 and the herring-reversing g9.r2.rev3.

Line 3363: the agent's own Analysis text states the (wrong) herring as a settled, 'Confirmed' fact just one turn after reading it, with no hedge -- contrast with its more careful, hedged treatment of the r1.rule conflict at line 2114.

The agent's added test suite (lines 4444-4719) reproduces several exact worked examples from remarks it found (the 33/99/100 Fireworks byte-budget numbers from say26; the window_start=51/39-length-weights numbers from say21), showing genuine synthesis of scattered numeric clues into working code -- just not for the two lost facts.

Mail search relied on 3 fixed IMAP terms (ExampleTooLongError, EncodingReport, last_report); widening that term list (e.g. adding 'supervised_tokens', 'token_count', 'role sequence') would likely have surfaced several more of the 7 missed mail remarks.
